contract.words: I want to clear $12,000 in profit — money kept after every cost — within 45 days. I can put up to $2,500 of my own money in, and I don't care which industry.

answers.finding: MAJOR: Paid orders before FULFILMENT is shown: add a step that secures a freelancer's written fixed quote <= $600 and a work sample before s3 takes payment.
answers.resolution: Accepted. New step s0 (day 1) obtains a written fixed quote <= $600 for the 5-page 7-day scope and a work sample before any offer; s3 now depends on s0, and the stop rule says no offer is sent if no such quote exists by day 3.

answers.finding: MAJOR: 'Delivered in 7 days' vs freelancer engaged only after each Stripe payout settles (day 10 sale delivered ~day 31); fund early builds from the $2,500 owner cap or restate the promise, and count refund risk.
answers.resolution: Accepted. Each freelancer is now paid the day after its sale; the first three builds (before the day-24 first payout) are funded from the owner's money, so peak owner money at risk is $400 + 3 x $600 = $2,200 inside the $2,500 cap, and every buyer gets delivery within 7 days of payment. One extra sale (11 instead of 10) is planned as slack against a refund.

answers.finding: MINOR: Step days (s5 28, s6 35, s7 42) do not match the ledger (receipts 10-27, builds 24-31).
answers.resolution: Accepted. Step days now match the ledger: s5 starts day 10 (first receipt), s6 day 11 (first build), s7 day 24 (first payout).

answers.finding: MINOR: members lists rejected openings cop_5fc8d0a3c9f34afd9582 and cop_26a54c7795b044ffa30f.
answers.resolution: Rebutted. Brain's check requires `members` arithmetic for every opening the plan weighs in `chain` (it returned ARITHMETIC_UNSTATED for both when they were omitted); they are weighed alternatives, not plan members, and the strategy's opportunityIds names only cop_f477d8f41fe44287b381.

answers.finding: NOTE: Sending from three brand-new secondary domains on day 3 skips the usual 2+ weeks of mailbox warm-up; deliverability for the day-14 gate is at risk, so the gate may stop a viable offer. Price $2,000 rests on agency estimates I verified are not buyer payments (cnd_b3215a31a4b54aeab4ad); fine only as what the test measures.
answers.resolution: Accepted in part. Warm-up starts day 1 and the first 1,000 contacts are spread over days 3-12 at warm-up-limited volume; the risk that the gate stops a viable offer is stated. Price stays an ESTIMATE that the test measures (OFFER_AND_PRICE is in validation.decides).

answers.finding: NOTE: The ledger books a $2,500 owner FUNDING on day 1 though only $400 is spent before receipts; harmless to profit but overstates owner money committed.
answers.resolution: Accepted. FUNDING is now $2,200: the $400 tools plus the three $600 builds advanced before the first payout.

answers.finding: FULFILMENT condition
answers.resolution: The card's fulfillment is a RECOMMENDATION and Brain's FULFILMENT link is false; s0 now secures a written quote and sample before any offer, and FULFILMENT stays in validation.decides.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right family and the arithmetic mostly holds: 10 x $2,000 = $20,000; costs $400 tools + 10 x $600 build + 10 x $58.30 Stripe = $6,983; profit $13,017 >= $12,000 (trace netCents 1301700), peak owner money at risk $400 << $2,500, last receipt settles day 31 of 45; the gate (2 paid of 1,000 = 0.2%) projected over the 5,000 planned contacts gives exactly the 10 sales needed, so passing at threshold carries the target (with no slack: 9 sales = $11,675). But: (1) The test takes buyers' money before fulfilment is shown possible. Brain's FULFILMENT link is false and the card's fulfillment is a RECOMMENDATION; the plan's own quantity says a freelancer's written fixed quote <= $600 is needed 'before the first sale is accepted', yet no step obtains it before s3 starts taking 100% up-front Stripe payments on day 3, and the stop branch is 'refund and stop'. Get the quote (and a sample of the freelancer's 5-page work) as a step before the offer goes out. (2) The delivery promise contradicts the ledger: the offer is 'delivered in 7 days', but each freelancer is engaged only once that sale's Stripe payout settles (sale 1 paid day 10, payout day 24, build to ~day 31), so early buyers wait ~3 weeks, inviting refunds/chargebacks that the ledger counts at $0. Either fund the first builds from owner money (each $600, inside the $2,500 cap) or change the promise. (3) Steps and ledger disagree: s5 SELL day 28, s6 DELIVER day 35, s7 COLLECT day 42, while receipts run days 10-27 and builds days 24-31. (4) members still carries the two rejected alternatives (25 GBP deals, 37 BrightLocal client-months) although the strategy names only cop_f477d8f41fe44287b381.
